findings.evidence: Lines 262-265: `have hsplit : (1 - z) • p = z • (((1 - z) / z) • p) := by rw [smul_smul]; congr 1; field_simp`; lines 447-450: `have hsplit : (1 - z) • p = ((1 - z) / z) • (z • p) := by rw [smul_smul]; congr 1; field_simp`.
findings.fix: State it once, e.g. `theorem one_sub_smul_eq_div_smul_smul {z : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) (p : V) : (1 - z) • p = ((1 - z) / z) • (z • p)`, proved with `match_scalars <;> field_simp`, and use it (plus `smul_comm`) at both sites; reuse it for the `(1 + t)⁻¹` step at 246-249.
findings.issue: The fragment-rescaling identity `(1 - z) • p = ((1 - z)/z) • (z • p)` for `0 < z` is proved inline twice, by the same `rw [smul_smul]; congr 1; field_simp` script: lines 262-265 (`hsplit` in `IsPosHomogeneous.isCollinearExactOn_of_merge_smul`) and lines 447-450 (`hsplit` in `IsCollinearExactOn.apply_smul_cons_one_sub_smul_cons`, with the arguments of `smul` swapped). The related inverse form appears a third time at lines 246-249 (`hmul`/`inv_smul_smul₀` in `merge_smul_eq_one_add_smul`). This hides the reusable fact that drives all three case analyses.

findings.evidence: Line 406: `simp only [smulScheme_merge, ← smul_add, smul_smul, mul_comm]`; line 400: `congr 1` + `abel`; line 386: `merge_comm a b := by rw [add_comm]`. `module` is used as a tactic at EpsilonEridani/QFT/Scattering/DIS/Tensors/Basic.lean:362.
findings.fix: Replace each with the robust tactic for linear identities: `module` (already used in this repo) or an anchored rewrite — `rw [smul_comm]` at 406, `module` at 400, `rw [add_comm a b]` at 386.
findings.issue: `isPosHomogeneous_smulScheme` is closed by putting `mul_comm` in a `simp only` list, so it works only because simp's ordered rewriting normalises `(c * d) • (a + b)` and `(d * c) • (a + b)` to the same term; nothing in the script records that the content is `smul_comm`. Same pattern of avoidable brittleness in `isAdditive_smulScheme` (line 400, `congr 1; abel` after `simp only [← smul_add]`) and `smulScheme.merge_comm` (line 386, `rw [add_comm]` with no explicit arguments, which rewrites whichever `a + b` subterm matches first).

summary: Proofs are readable and free of defeq abuse, but one reusable rescaling identity is duplicated across two proofs and the smulScheme lemmas close linear identities by simp term-ordering and unanchored rewrites instead of stating the step.
